Fee compression; regulatory notes: Surplus recovery fee caps, assignment validity and waiting periods vary.; Court filings may require licensed counsel.; track ids: track_1; track labels: Asymmetric & Data-Arbitrage Plays; plays: id: public_record_api_intelligence; track id: track_1; name: Public-Record & API Intelligence; mechanism: Ingest fragmented county dockets, probate registries, unclaimed property ledgers, and public APIs to surface uncontested claims or high-intent B2B triggers before manual competitors.; inputs: Court & probate dockets; State controller ledgers; Public licensing & entity APIs; workflow: Poll and normalize county/state record releases on an automated cadence; Cross-match entity/kinship/lien records and filter by minimum net fee threshold; Route verified dossiers into compliant outreach and claim execution; metrics: Cost per verified lead; Docket-to-contact latency (hours); Net recovery / conversion rate; platform risks: failure mode: Portal rate-limiting or CAPTCHA gating; trigger: High-frequency automated polling against county or agency web portals; impact: Delayed lead ingestion or temporary IP block on target registry; detection metric: HTTP 429/403 rate and daily record ingestion delta; fallback: Switch to scheduled bulk FOIA/public-record exports, official data feeds, and low-frequency cached queues; id: distressed_asset_recovery; track id: track_1; name: Distressed Asset Recovery; mechanism: Locate mispriced, orphaned, or administratively stranded assets—tax-sale overages, unclaimed state funds, dormant judgments, government surplus lots, or distressed micro-businesses—and capture a contingent recovery fee or acquisition spread.; inputs: Tax-sale excess proceeds ledgers; Unclaimed property & judgment dockets; Surplus auction manifests; workflow: Audit statutory fee caps, claim windows, and chain-of-title encumbrances; Execute skip-tracing or asset inspection to confirm net realizable value; Lock in contingent recovery agreements or below-intrinsic buyouts; metrics: Gross spread / contingent fee per case; Claim approval rate; Days from filing to disbursement; platform risks: failure mode: Statutory fee-cap compression or administrative hold; trigger: Jurisdiction updates finder fee limits, waiting periods, or filing documentation rules; impact: Reduced net fee margin or extended cash conversion cycle; detection metric: County/state rejection notice rate and days-to-payout variance; fallback: Diversify across multi-state dockets and use attorney-backed filing partnerships where required; id: unclaimed_property_escheatment_arbitrage; track id: track_1; name: State Treasury Escheatment & Unclaimed Corporate Warrant Recovery; mechanism: Ingest state controller/treasury escheatment ledgers and uncashed municipal/corporate warrant registries above $25,000, cross-match corporate officers via Secretary of State filings, and execute statutory recovery agreements for a 10–25% contingent finder fee.; inputs: State controller/treasury escheatment bulk ledgers; Uncashed municipal warrant & vendor-credit registries; Secretary of State officer & FEIN cross-match index; workflow: Filter state unclaimed-property and uncashed-warrant ledgers for high-value corporate and estate accounts exceeding $25,000; Resolve active corporate officers, successor entities, or authorized fiduciaries via SOS and skip-trace databases; Execute state-compliant finder agreements with statutory fee caps and submit notarized claim packages to the treasury administrator; metrics: Average gross warrant/escheatment claim size ($25k+); Treasury claim approval rate (%); Days from notarized filing to state disbursement; platform risks: failure mode: Statutory finder-fee cap violation or waiting-period rejection; trigger: Charging above state statutory fee limits (e.g., 10% in CA/FL/NY) or soliciting claims during restricted post-escheatment windows; impact: Voided recovery contract, state controller rejection, or administrative penalty; detection metric: State-by-state fee-cap compliance check (100% pass) and claim rejection notice rate; fallback: Enforce per-state statutory fee caps and waiting-period rules in intake templates and disclose the owner's right to claim directly for free; id: probate_docket_inheritance_arbitrage; track id: track_1; name: Probate Docket & Pre-Foreclosure Notice-of-Default (NOD) Scraping; mechanism: Parse county probate petitions (Letters Testamentary / Letters of Administration) and daily Notice-of-Default (NOD) filings before national aggregators index them, matching out-of-state personal representatives and distressed owners to licensed probate brokers and cash buyers.; inputs: County probate court register of actions & Letters Testamentary filings; County recorder daily Notice-of-Default (NOD) & Notice-of-Trustee-Sale feeds; Skip-tracing & out-of-state personal-representative matching pipeline; workflow: Extract newly appointed estate personal representatives and real-property inventory from county probate dockets within 24 hours of filing; Cross-match parcel equity and mortgage balances against county assessor and recorder records; Deliver empathetic estate-liquidation checklists, property-preservation referrals, or licensed brokerage introductions; metrics: Docket-to-first-contact speed vs. national data aggregators (days); Personal-representative response & appointment rate (%); Commission or referral fee per closed probate/pre-foreclosure parcel; platform risks: failure mode: State Foreclosure Consultant Act violations or unlicensed brokerage fee-splitting; trigger: Charging upfront fees to distressed homeowners in NOD or taking unlicensed real-estate commission splits; impact: Voided contracts, treble damages under state foreclosure-protection statutes, or DRE enforcement; detection metric: 100% licensed broker co-marketing compliance and zero upfront homeowner fee charges; fallback: Monetize strictly via flat-fee marketing/data subscriptions to licensed probate agents or close transactions through a licensed brokerage of record; id: property_tax_assessment_appeal_contingency; track id: track_1; name: Automated Commercial/Residential Property-Tax Appeal Arbitrage; mechanism: Ingest county tax-assessor valuation rolls upon annual notice release, run an automated valuation model (AVM) flagging parcels assessed above comparable neighbor equity ratios, and file bulk administrative tax protests for 30–50% of the first year's verified tax reduction.; inputs: Annual county tax-assessor preliminary valuation rolls & parcel GIS characteristics; Equity-ratio & recent-sale comparable AVM engine; Bulk administrative ARB (Appraisal Review Board) protest filing & hearing pipeline; workflow: Ingest county assessment rolls the day annual valuation notices drop and compute each parcel's assessed-per-sqft percentile against direct neighborhood peers; Mail personalized pre-filled protest postcards showing the owner's exact estimated over-assessment and a QR code to sign a zero-upfront-cost contingency authorization; Auto-generate uniform comparable-equity evidence packets, file bulk administrative protests before the county bar date, and collect 30–50% of Year-1 tax savings; metrics: Protest-window mail-to-signed-authorization conversion %; Percentage of appealed parcels receiving an assessment reduction (65–85% target); Average net contingency fee per residential ($150–$450) and commercial ($2,000–$15,000) parcel; platform risks: failure mode: State property-tax consultant licensing requirements or missed county protest bar dates; trigger: Representing property owners for a fee without required state registration (e.g., Texas TDLR Property Tax Consultant license) or missing the 30/45-day county filing deadline; impact: Rejected bulk filings, administrative fines, or zero contingency revenue for the tax year; detection metric: 100% licensed tax-agent sign-off in regulated states and T-minus-7-day bulk filing completion; fallback: Partner with licensed local property-tax consultants/attorneys of record in regulated states and automate pre-deadline batch electronic filing; id: hoa_super_lien_tax_deed_redemption_arbitrage; track id: track_1; name: HOA Super-Lien & Sub-Threshold Tax-Deed Statutory Redemption Arbitrage; mechanism: Price small HOA priority liens and tax-sale interests using jurisdiction-specific priority, notice, and redemption rules; returns depend on enforceable rights, not assumed title extinguishment.; inputs: County tax-sale and HOA lien records; Title report and statutory redemption calendar; Local counsel priority and notice opinion; workflow: 1. Screen small-balance liens against property value, senior debt, and sale eligibility; 2. Have local counsel verify priority, service, redemption rights, and purchaser restrictions; 3. Bid within a net-recovery ceiling and calendar every payment and notice deadline; 4. Reconcile redemption proceeds or pursue counsel-supervised title resolution after rights expire; metrics: Net realized recovery after legal costs; Capital days outstanding; Notice and redemption deadline compliance rate; platform risks: failure mode: Sale invalidation or surviving senior lien; trigger: Defective notice or incorrect assumption about statutory lien priority; impact: Loss of expected recovery and extended title litigation; detection metric: Unresolved title exceptions and notice defects per acquisition; fallback: Suspend bidding, seek available statutory refunds, and limit acquisitions to counsel-cleared interests; platform risks: failure mode: Portal rate-limiting or CAPTCHA gating; trigger: High-frequency automated polling against county or agency web portals; impact: Delayed lead ingestion or temporary IP block on target registry; detection metric: HTTP 429/403 rate and daily record ingestion delta; fallback: Switch to scheduled bulk FOIA/public-record exports, official data feeds, and low-frequency cached queues; play id: public_record_api_intelligence; play name: Public-Record & API Intelligence;
